title: OPTIMIZING ACOUSTIC DESIGN AND SCHEMATIC ARCHITECTURAL LAYOUTS OF OFFICE BUILDINGS
target_construct: Optimizing acoustic design decisions and automating thematic architectural layout generation for office buildings

findings.antecedent: Novel optimization model for acoustic design decisions
findings.consequent: Minimizes cost of acoustic materials while achieving designer-specified acoustic quality requirements
findings.source: Abstract; Chapter 3.2 Objective; Chapter 3.8 Summary and Conclusions; Chapter 5.2 Research Contributions
findings.validation_evidence: Real-world application example showed $13,545 total cost, significantly lower than industry estimates ($15,000-$25,000).

findings.antecedent: Novel optimization model for acoustic design decisions
findings.consequent: Identifies optimal acoustic material selections (type and area) for each floor, ceiling, and wall in office spaces
findings.source: Chapter 3.8 Summary and Conclusions; Chapter 5.2 Research Contributions
findings.validation_evidence: Demonstrated through a real-world application example (Table 3.4).

findings.antecedent: Innovative methodology for automating thematic architectural layout generation using nature-inspired images
findings.consequent: Automates the generation of optimal thematic architectural layouts for the schematic design phase
findings.source: Abstract; Chapter 4.2 Research Objective; Chapter 4.11 Summary and conclusion; Chapter 5.2 Research Contributions
findings.validation_evidence: Application example generated layouts for two images in 54 and 44 seconds respectively, with positive architect feedback on efficiency.

findings.antecedent: Novel region and boundary extraction algorithm (part of layout methodology)
findings.consequent: Subdivides segmented images into regions and identifies boundaries by scanning pixels
findings.source: Chapter 4.4 Region and Boundary Extraction; Chapter 5.2 Research Contributions

findings.antecedent: Novel algorithm for region refinement (part of layout methodology)
findings.consequent: Removes narrow regions that are too small to be classified as a room by merging them with adjacent larger regions
findings.source: Chapter 4.5.1 Removal of narrow regions algorithm; Chapter 5.2 Research Contributions

findings.antecedent: Original algorithm for region refinement (part of layout methodology)
findings.consequent: Subdivides large regions using horizontal and vertical cuts based on designer-specified threshold to achieve required room count
findings.source: Chapter 4.5.2 Subdivide large regions; Chapter 5.2 Research Contributions

findings.antecedent: Room assignment optimization algorithm (part of layout methodology)
findings.consequent: Optimizes room assignments to maximize compliance with designer-specified adjacency requirements
findings.source: Chapter 4.6 Room assignment optimization; Chapter 4.11 Summary and conclusion; Chapter 5.2 Research Contributions
findings.validation_evidence: Application example achieved 71% (Image 1) and 64% (Image 2) compliance with adjacency requirements.

findings.antecedent: Room area optimization algorithm (part of layout methodology)
findings.consequent: Optimizes room areas to minimize the total mismatch between target and layout areas while complying with image theme and room adjacency constraints
findings.source: Chapter 4.7 Room area optimization; Chapter 4.11 Summary and conclusion; Chapter 5.2 Research Contributions
findings.validation_evidence: Application example achieved 89% (Image 1) and 92% (Image 2) compliance with room area requirements.

findings.antecedent: Room boundaries smoothing algorithm (part of layout methodology)
findings.consequent: Smoothens all boundaries of each room to create practical architectural layouts
findings.source: Chapter 4.8 Room boundaries smoothing; Chapter 4.11 Summary and conclusion

findings.antecedent: First nature-inspired image (staghorn fern leaf pattern)
findings.consequent: Generated optimal layout with 71% compliance for adjacency requirements and 89% compliance for room areas
findings.source: Chapter 4.9 Application example; Chapter 4.11 Summary and conclusion
findings.validation_evidence: 30 out of 42 adjacency requirements met; 11% total area mismatch.

findings.antecedent: Second nature-inspired image (soap bubbles/organic cells pattern)
findings.consequent: Generated optimal layout with 64% compliance for adjacency requirements and 92% compliance for room areas
findings.source: Chapter 4.9 Application example; Chapter 4.11 Summary and conclusion
findings.validation_evidence: 27 out of 42 adjacency requirements met; 8% total area mismatch.

findings.antecedent: First image's theme and pattern (more adjacencies)
findings.consequent: Outperformed the second image in compliance with room adjacency requirements (average 2.7 vs 2.4 adjacencies)

findings.antecedent: Second image's theme and pattern (better area fit)
findings.consequent: Was superior in its compliance with room area requirements

components.name: Acoustic Quality Optimization Model
components.description: A model to minimize the cost of acoustic materials in office spaces while complying with designer-specified acoustic quality requirements, using genetic algorithms.
components.validation: Evaluated using a real-world office building example, demonstrating cost savings compared to industry estimates.

components.name: Automation Optimization Methodology for Thematic Architectural Layouts
components.description: A methodology to automate the generation of optimal thematic architectural layout designs inspired by nature images.
components.validation: Evaluated using two nature-inspired images, demonstrating efficient generation and optimization of room assignments and areas.

components.name: Image Segmentation Stage
components.description: Converts input image to a 2D array of pixels and segments it into foreground/background regions using a Threshold binary algorithm.

components.name: Region and Boundary Extraction Algorithm
components.description: Subdivides the segmented image into regions and identifies their boundaries based on color intensity differences between adjacent pixels.

components.name: Narrow Region Removal Algorithm
components.description: Identifies and removes small, impractical narrow regions by merging them with adjacent larger regions, using vertical/horizontal scan lines and boundary loop detection.

components.name: Large Region Subdivision Algorithm
components.description: Divides large regions using horizontal or vertical cuts if the number of formed regions is less than the designer-specified requirement.

components.name: Room Assignment Optimization Algorithm
components.description: Optimizes the assignment of required rooms to extracted regions to maximize compliance with designer-specified adjacency requirements, by grouping rooms and regions and generating combinations.
components.validation: Demonstrated in application example with compliance scores.

components.name: Room Area Optimization Algorithm
components.description: Optimizes the areas of assigned rooms to minimize the total mismatch between target and layout areas, while preserving image theme and adjacency, using a gradient-based optimization algorithm.
components.validation: Demonstrated in application example with area compliance scores.

components.name: Room Boundaries Smoothing Algorithm
components.description: Smoothens non-smooth broken lines of room boundaries by creating boundary segments using DFS and applying piecewise linear approximation.

recommended_use: To support architects, designers, and decision-makers in optimizing acoustic design decisions (material selection, cost minimization) and automating the generation of optimal thematic architectural layouts (room assignment, area optimization, boundary smoothing) during the schematic design phase of office buildings.
limitations: Does not consider designer-specified minimum width, length, and degree angle for rooms to improve functionality and avoid narrow rooms.
Does not account for designer-specified dimensions of building and/or project site layout.
Does not enable the creation of thematic layouts for buildings with multiple floors, including elevator and stairway locations.
Does not transform the generated 2D schematic layout to a 3D model for improved visualization.
Does not prioritize the compliance of rooms/zones with designer-specified area requirements based on their relative importance during room area optimization.
Acoustic quality model could be expanded to a multi-objective optimization model to maximize acoustic quality measures while minimizing building noise control cost (including installation cost).
Acoustic quality model could be expanded to calculate flanking noise caused by HVAC systems, small spaces around doors/windows, and vertically generated noise from multiple floors.
Layout methodology could be expanded to incorporate architectural layout format details (lines thickness, doors, windows) for the design development phase.

Layout methodology could be expanded to generate optimal layouts for multiple floors considering building structure, short path exits, and natural lighting to improve design functionality and efficiency.
